pass_line: Each object must beat the raw baselines-margin__street object on MAE for BOTH adj_ebitda_musd and adj_ebitda_margin_pct, at h=0 AND h=1, in W1 AND W2, on BOTH weightings (equal mae and rw_mae), PIT replay, matched quarters. An object failing any cell fails the pass line and is written up as a failure, not deleted.
secondary_tests: Ljung-Box Q(4) on the h=0 margin surprise series (n<=22): power is low; reported, not a gate.

Quarter-of-year seasonality of the surprise: pooled OLS F-test on quarter dummies; the seasonal bias variant is used ONLY if p<0.10 on the W2-era sample. Default expectation: fails, pooled bias is used.
FY-floor anchoring: Street FY margin at each guide date vs the FY floor in force (replication of WS03 with the harness guide table).
Dispersion regression: |margin surprise| and margin surprise on ebitda_sd/ebitda_mean at the vintage.

parameters_fixed_before_fitting.estimation_pool_rationale: 2021 is the COVID re-opening regime: the Street had a -50.7% margin estimate for 1Q21 and the realised surprise was +44.0 pt (WS03 surprise table). Averaging that into a 2024 bias is not a point-in-time judgement about the same object. Pool starts at 2022Q1. Sensitivity spec rw_hl4_from21 keeps 2021 and is registered alongside.

notes: Street quarterly consensus exists at h=0 and h=1 only (WS03 roles guided_q_pre_guide / next_q_pre_guide). Backtest horizons are therefore h=0 and h=1; no h=2 row can be built. LIVE 1Q27-4Q27 Street is derived by allocating the FY27 consensus across quarters with the harness PIT seasonal EBITDA shares (spec_id suffix _fyalloc, documented, never used in a scored backtest cell).

spec_notes.rw_hl4: primary: exponential weights half-life 4 q, shrunk mean; % bias for the $ target, pt bias for margin
spec_notes.rw_hl4_usd: additive $ bias for adj_ebitda_musd instead of multiplicative %
spec_notes.rw_hl4_med: recency-weighted MEDIAN surprise instead of the mean (robust to the 2021-22 tail), same shrinkage
spec_notes.rw_hl4_from21: primary rule but the estimation pool starts at 2021Q1
